## Structure and components

- [statement] ICE (parent of the New York Stock Exchange) agreed with Trade XYZ to bring Trade XYZ's Hyperliquid perpetual futures to the US, pending regulatory approval. ICE would be the exclusive operator of Trade XYZ's regulated markets and intends to establish a new, dedicated, regulated retail market and clearing structure. Galaxy Research notes that US traders will get a separate, permissioned venue with its own clearing, and that the liquidity will not be shared with the existing HIP-3 markets, meaning the US venue will start from zero. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-29) — https://ir.theice.com/press/news-details/2026/Intercontinental-Exchange-and-TradeXYZ-to-Bring-Hyperliquid-Based-Perpetual-Markets-Onshore/ · keywords: US-person access to perpetuals and US-regulated perp fees · also: https://www.galaxy.com/insights/research/nyse-parent-signs-deal-to-bring-compliant-hyperliquid-perps-to-u-s

## How it works

- [statement] Bitnomial provides two methods for connecting and trading on the Exchange: Direct and Indirect. Direct Market Access (DMA) provides low-latency connectivity through private network connections, with AWS PrivateLink as the primary option. Its Binary (BTP) API is a low latency binary protocol for order entry and price feeds. The REST API is rate-limited to 200 requests per 5 minutes, and exceeding this rate results in HTTP 403 responses. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://bitnomial.com/exchange/docs/api/overview/ · keywords: US-person access to perpetuals and US-regulated perp fees · also: https://bitnomial.com/exchange/docs/api/rest/overview/, https://bitnomial.com/exchange/docs/api/rest/orders/, https://bitnomial.com/exchange/docs/api/connection-ids/
- [statement] Hyperliquid enforces its US restriction at the front end, not the chain. As of November 2, 2026 the frontend at app.hyperliquid.xyz still showed its restricted-jurisdiction banner to a US connection, and the Terms of Service still restricted use by US persons. The L1 protocol underneath does not perform this check; it processes signed transactions from any wallet. Per the guide, Hyperliquid's own Terms of Service are the actual restriction, and the frontend IP check is one mechanism for enforcing them. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-02) — https://hyperliquidguide.com/privacy/hyperliquid-us-availability · keywords: US-person access to perpetuals and US-regulated perp fees · also: https://app.hyperliquid.xyz/terms

- [statement] Coinbase Financial Markets has offered US customers CFTC-regulated perpetual futures since July 21, 2025 (nano Bitcoin and nano Ether at launch), with up to 10x intraday leverage on crypto. Coinbase's own announcement says fees are as low as 0.02% per contract. - [statement] Kalshi's perpetual futures fee schedule (submitted August 4, 2026, effective not before August 18, 2026) sets taker fees from 0.0400% at tier 0 down to 0.0100% at >= $1,000M of trailing perps plus prediction volume, and maker fees from 0.0200% at tier 0 to 0.0000% from >= $10M. The amended fee schedule applies the existing self-clearing member fee schedule to traders executing orders through an FCM; a proposed change filed on June 24, 2026 (charging a fee to FCM customers) did not take effect. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-08-04) — https://www.cftc.gov/filings/orgrules/rules08042613787.pdf
- [statement] Kalshi's Temporary Perpetual Fee Rebate Program update (implemented on or after 5:00 PM ET on August 18, 2026) covers all Self-Clearing Members of Kalshi. Taker fees will be rebated down to 0.3 bps (0.003%) and makers net 0.3 bps (0.003%). The update remains in effect until the earlier of December 31, 2026, or a date on which Kalshi amends or terminates the Program, and Kalshi may end the Program at any time with one week's notice to all exchange participants. ## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Crypto.com's US perps trade on a CFTC-regulated exchange and clearinghouse that does business in the Crypto.com App under the brand Crypto.com | Derivatives North America (CDNA) and in a separate trader-focused App, with leverage up to 5x, and the final funding rate cannot be higher than +2% or lower than −2% for an eight-hour interval. Foris DAX Inc is the entity registered with NFA as an introducing broker. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-27) — https://robinhood.com/newsroom/robinhood-cryptocom/ · keywords: US-person access to perpetuals and US-regulated perp fees · also: https://crypto.com/en/product-news/crypto-perpetuals-launch, https://help.crypto.com/en/articles/17741688-perpetual-trading-in-the-us, https://crypto.com/en/company-news/ogcom-and-cryptocom-expand-derivatives-offering-with-launch-of-regulated-crypto-perpetuals-for-the-us-market
- [statement] Kalshi's Perps API mirrors its event-contract API under a `/margin` namespace, with endpoints for account balance and risk, funding (estimated and historical rates, plus payment history), fee tiers, subaccounts, and transfers between event-contract and margin balances. Production endpoints are 'rolling out member by member', with REST on the `external-api` hosts and WebSocket and FIX on separate perps hosts. The event-contract to margin transfer is not yet available (enabled with the production rollout), and `/margin/enabled` shows whether margin is on for an account. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.kalshi.com/margin
- [statement] Gibson Dunn says the risk controls it describes are principally associated with offshore and onchain trading venues, which generally are not available to US persons. CoinGape says Binance Futures, Bybit, Deribit, and OKX's international derivatives platform restrict US residents from using their international futures services. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-16) — https://www.gibsondunn.com/perpetual-contracts-product-structure-and-recent-us-regulatory-developments/ · keywords: US-person access to perpetuals and US-regulated perp fees · also: https://coingape.com/crypto-exchanges/futures/
- [statement] US-based Kalshi users who have completed KYC verification are eligible to apply for perps access, and international availability may expand in the future. Applying involves a margin account application with a short questionnaire about trading experience and risk tolerance. Most retail users trade perpetuals currently through Kalshi Prime, a registered Futures Commission Merchant (FCM), while institutional participants may become Self-Clearing Members and clear directly with Kalshi Klear. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://help.kalshi.com/en/articles/15357656-applying-for-perpetuals-access · keywords: US-person access to perpetuals and US-regulated perp fees · also: https://kalshi.com/perpetuals/learn/what-are-perpetual-futures
- [statement] Kalshi documents a Perps API under a `/margin` namespace that mirrors its event-contract API. The production REST base URL is `https://external-api.kalshi.com/trade-api/v2/margin/` (rolling out member by member); WebSocket and FIX use separate perps hosts, and a lower-latency host serves fill and user_orders updates. Margin endpoints cover account balance and risk, funding (estimated and historical rates, plus payment history), fee tiers, and subaccounts. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.kalshi.com/margin · keywords: US-person access to perpetuals and US-regulated perp fees · also: https://docs.kalshi.com/getting_started/quick_start_authenticated_requests, https://github.com/hummingbot/hummingbot/blob/3351adad0a09f6a57a202219d3e52fe794672421/hummingbot/connector/derivative/kalshi_perpetual/kalshi_perpetual_constants.py, https://github.com/pmxt-dev/pmxt/issues/1998

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] CME filed suit on June 18, 2026 in the US District Court for the District of Columbia against the CFTC, challenging the May 29, 2026 order approving Kalshi's BTCPERP and the Policy Statement. If CME prevails, the court could vacate the Kalshi Order and Policy Statement and declare that digital commodity Perpetuals are 'swaps' rather than 'futures' under the CEA. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-06-18) — https://www.legal500.com/intelligence/united-states/finance-and-banking/fctm-breaking-news-cme-sues-cftc-over-approval-of-bitcoin-perpetual-futures-contract · keywords: US-person access to perpetuals and US-regulated perp fees · also: https://www.mcdermottlaw.com/insights/cftc-signals-regulation-shift-as-cme-challenges-classification-of-perpetuals-as-futures/
- [statement] CFTC Chairman Michael Selig said crypto onchain platforms looking to offer derivatives to US retail traders can register as an exchange or partner with one that is already registered, pointing to Backpack, which earlier that week received three licenses for its US entry, as an example of the first route. He also explained why the agency considers single-stock perpetuals futures rather than swaps, saying funding payments are very similar to variation margin with other types of futures contracts and the contracts are structured as futures, not as a swap or a security-based swap. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-19) — https://www.theblock.co/news/regulation/2026-11-19-cftc-chair-selig-hyperliquid-onchain-venues-the-us-444106 · keywords: US-person access to perpetuals and US-regulated perp fees · also: https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/11/16/3404185/0/en/backpack-receives-landmark-cftc-approval-to-establish-first-ever-blockchain-based-derivatives-exchange-in-the-united-states-with-global-unified-liquidity.html
- [statement] Kalshi perp fees depend on account route. Kalshi's CFTC fee-schedule filing sets taker fees from 0.0400% at tier 0 to 0.0100% at >= $1,000M of 30D trailing perps plus prediction volume and maker fees from 0.0200% at tier 0 to 0.0000% from >= $10M, and says this section is available to all self-clearing members of the exchange. A third-party read of the live Base-rate selections displayed different taker schedules for Prime and self-clearing: below $100,000, Prime was 0.120% /12 bps taker and 0.020% /2 bps maker versus self-clearing 0.040% /4 bps taker and 0.020% /2 bps maker. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-21) — https://www.cftc.gov/filings/orgrules/rules08042613787.pdf · keywords: US-person access to perpetuals and US-regulated perp fees · also: https://www.alphascope.app/blog/kalshi-perps-fees, https://kalshi.com/docs/kalshi-fee-schedule.pdf
- [statement] A single-author SSRN preprint reports that Kalshi launched the first CFTC-regulated perpetual futures on 3 June 2026, and that through 20 September 2026 39% of BTC and 48% of ETH notional was executed in resting quotes of a fixed dollar size taken in full by orders of the same size. When the fee schedule went live on 24 June, venue-wide volume collapsed by 80-92% within hours and returned about forty hours later with ticket volume three to five times higher. The author says the evidence is consistent with volume that exists because it is costless to produce rather than because it serves a trading purpose. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-22) — https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=7512338 · keywords: US-person access to perpetuals and US-regulated perp fees · also: https://www.desilvalawoffices.com/articles/blog/2026/september/cme-perpetual-futures-lawsuit-cftc-moves-to-dism/
- [statement] An SSRN working paper finds that through 20 September 2026 (26.3 million trades, $47.2 billion) 39% of BTC and 48% of ETH notional was executed in resting quotes of a fixed dollar size taken in full by orders of the same size. When the fee schedule went live on 24 June, venue-wide volume collapsed by 80-92% within hours and returned about forty hours later with ticket volume three to five times higher; the metals contracts show no fixed-size flow. The author says the evidence is consistent with volume that exists because it is costless to produce rather than because it serves a trading purpose. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-22) — https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/Delivery.cfm?abstractid=7512338

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Hyperliquid's Terms of Use (clause 1.6) bar 'Restricted Persons', defined to include persons or entities that reside in, are located in, are incorporated in or have a registered office in the United States of America or Ontario, Canada. Reuters likewise reports that offshore platforms like Hyperliquid typically try to restrict US users. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://app.hyperliquid.xyz/terms · keywords: US-person access to perpetuals and US-regulated perp fees · also: https://www.reuters.com/legal/government/crypto-exchanges-gear-up-launch-us-perpetual-futures-ahead-rule-change-2026-04-22/
- [statement] Hyperliquid does not currently offer its trading platform to US users and enforces geo-blocking for US and Ontario, Canada residents; Hyperliquid Policy Center CEO Jake Chervinsky said the goal is for regulators to interpret existing rules favourably or create new ones that would allow regulated firms to offer perpetual futures using markets built on Hyperliquid. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-08-12) — https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/crypto/articles/hyperliquid-turns-cftc-path-u-153400685.html · keywords: US-person access to perpetuals and US-regulated perp fees · also: https://cryptobriefing.com/hyperliquid-us-perpetual-contracts-compliance/
- [statement] Hyperliquid co-founder and CEO Jeff Yan said that Americans using a VPN to access the exchange violate its terms of service, and that legal US access depends on regulators deciding that onchain technology fits CFTC principles. A VPN therefore creates a terms breach, not legal access. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-19) — https://247wallst.com/investing/cryptocurrency/2026/10/19/hyperliquids-ceo-explained-how-americans-could-legally-use-it-what-would-us-access-mean-for-hype/ · keywords: US-person access to perpetuals and US-regulated perp fees · also: https://app.hyperliquid.xyz/terms
- [statement] Paradex's Restricted Persons page excludes the United States (plus US associated territories such as Puerto Rico, Guam and the US Virgin Islands), Canada, and any 'US person' as defined under US securities and commodity futures laws; users represent on an ongoing basis that they are not a Restricted Person. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://www.paradex.trade/restricted-persons
- [statement] On May 29, 2026 the CFTC approved KalshiEX's bitcoin perpetual contract BTCPERP as a futures contract under Section 5c(c)(4) and Regulation 40.3. The same day it issued a policy statement on listing perpetual contracts, a staff advisory on 24/7 trading and clearing, and an interpretive letter and no-action position for Coinbase Financial Markets (CFTC Letter No. 26-17). (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-05-29) — https://www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/PressReleases/9240-26 · keywords: US-person access to perpetuals and US-regulated perp fees · also: https://www.lowenstein.com/news-insights/publications/client-alerts/fctm-breaking-news-cftc-approves-us-bitcoin-perpetual-futures-contract-and-issues-related-guidance-fctm, https://www.marketsmedia.com/cftc-approves-kalshiex-coinbase-perpetual-contracts/
- [statement] The CFTC policy statement encourages DCMs that wish to list perpetual contracts referencing asset classes not covered by the Order (such as agricultural products, precious metals, equity securities, narrow-based security indexes) to voluntarily submit them for Regulation 40.3 review and approval. The BTCPERP contract approved is a perpetual contract that references the spot price of bitcoin. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-05-29) — https://www.lowenstein.com/news-insights/publications/client-alerts/fctm-breaking-news-cftc-approves-us-bitcoin-perpetual-futures-contract-and-issues-related-guidance-fctm · keywords: US-person access to perpetuals and US-regulated perp fees · also: https://www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/PressReleases/9240-26
- [statement] A CFTC interpretive letter confirms that Deribit FZE perpetuals (Deribit is an affiliated foreign board of trade regulated by the Dubai Virtual Assets Regulatory Authority) may be categorized as 'foreign futures' under Regulation 30.1, letting Coinbase Financial Markets offer US customers access to them. The interpretation is limited to perpetual contracts structured similarly to the Deribit Perpetuals and based on digital commodities with deep, active, and continuous spot market trading. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-05-29) — https://www.lowenstein.com/news-insights/publications/client-alerts/fctm-breaking-news-cftc-approves-us-bitcoin-perpetual-futures-contract-and-issues-related-guidance-fctm · keywords: US-person access to perpetuals and US-regulated perp fees · also: https://www.marketsmedia.com/cftc-approves-kalshiex-coinbase-perpetual-contracts/
- [statement] In an April report, Reuters described US perps as being in a regulatory gray area, neither banned nor explicitly approved. It said Bitnomial is the only US platform offering perpetual futures via self-certification and that Coinbase self-certified 'perpetual-style' futures with five-year expiration dates and leverage of up to 10 times; Kraken's parent company was acquiring Bitnomial for up to $550 million. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-04-22) — https://www.reuters.com/legal/government/crypto-exchanges-gear-up-launch-us-perpetual-futures-ahead-rule-change-2026-04-22/ · keywords: US-person access to perpetuals and US-regulated perp fees · also: https://blog.kraken.com/product/kraken-derivatives/announcing-cftc-regulated-us-perps
- [statement] Kraken launched CFTC-regulated US perpetual futures on Kraken Pro; the contracts are listed on Bitnomial (owned by Kraken's parent Payward), and Kraken's support page lists 16 contracts at launch (for example PBTCUC). Bitnomial's self-certification shows PBTCUC is a cash-settled perpetual futures contract with a contract size of 0.01 BTC referenced to the CF Bitcoin Mid-Price Spot Rate. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) — https://blog.kraken.com/product/kraken-derivatives/announcing-cftc-regulated-us-perps · keywords: US-person access to perpetuals and US-regulated perp fees · also: https://support.kraken.com/articles/us-perpetual-futures, https://www.cftc.gov/filings/ptc/ptc0514263381.pdf
- [statement] Kraken Derivatives US charges a flat per-contract all-in fee of $0.0113 per side for Bitnomial-listed perps ($0.0003 commission + $0.001 exchange/clearing + $0.01 NFA); round-turn is double. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) — https://support.kraken.com/articles/us-futures-fees
- [statement] Bitnomial describes its perps as replicating the full economic design of offshore perpetuals, on the same unified exchange and clearinghouse as futures, options and spot, and as the first and only CFTC-regulated exchange accepting digital assets as margin collateral. Its API surface is reported (by a third-party API directory profile) as a real-time WebSocket market-data feed, a low-latency binary order-entry protocol (BTP), and a FIX 4.4 API with dropcopy, with REST authentication using HMAC-SHA256 request signing. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://bitnomial.com/market/perpetuals · keywords: US-person access to perpetuals and US-regulated perp fees · also: https://apis.io/providers/bitnomial/
- [statement] Hyperliquid enforces the US restriction at its web frontend. As of November 2, 2026 the frontend at app.hyperliquid.xyz still showed its restricted-jurisdiction banner to a US connection, and the Terms govern the website-hosted Interface. One affiliate guide adds that the L1 protocol itself does not perform IP-based geo-blocking, a distinction it calls purely technical that does not amount to a statement about what is or is not permitted. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-02) — https://hyperliquidguide.com/privacy/hyperliquid-us-availability · keywords: US-person access to perpetuals and US-regulated perp fees · also: https://app.hyperliquid.xyz/terms
